subject.title: RFC: policy on agent-directed instruction content in docs

question: Should ClawHub publish an acceptability boundary for agent-directed instructions in SKILL.md/README content, and where should that rule live?
rationale: The request defines a marketplace trust boundary; current main only provides adjacent scanner and acceptable-use concepts, so automation should not choose the final public policy line.

options.title: Adopt Public Policy Guidance
options.body: Add concise allowed, needs-review, and not-allowed examples to public acceptable-use or publishing docs and mirror the invariant in specs.

options.title: Fold Into Related RFCs
options.body: Resolve this only together with the capability-manifest and cross-asset review RFCs so schema, scanner signals, and policy wording ship together.

options.title: Keep Boundary Internal
options.body: Leave this to ClawScan and moderator judgment for now, accepting less predictability for submitters.

recommendation.title: Adopt Public Policy Guidance
recommendation.body: Add concise allowed, needs-review, and not-allowed examples to public acceptable-use or publishing docs and mirror the invariant in specs.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle is the strongest routing signal from CODEOWNERS and blame for the affected security docs and ClawScan prompt paths.
